name: IRCoT - Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
venue: ACL 2023 (Long Paper; ACL Anthology 2023.acl-long.557). Preprint arXiv:2212.10509 (submitted Dec 2022, v2 Jun 2023).
authors_affiliation: Harsh Trivedi, Niranjan Balasubramanian (Stony Brook University); Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal (Allen Institute for AI / AI2).
task_domain: QA - knowledge-intensive multi-step (multi-hop) open-domain question answering.
problem_setting: Few-shot (in-context, no additional training) open-domain multi-step QA over a large external corpus, following a retrieve-and-read paradigm. Single-agent, offline non-interactive inference. The key observation is that for multi-step QA, what to retrieve depends on what has already been derived, which in turn depends on what was previously retrieved, so one-step question-based retrieve-and-read is insufficient. Supervision is limited to ~20 hand-written CoT exemplars per dataset (used as in-context demonstrations); no parameter updates are made to the LLM or retriever.
what_is_retrieved: Documents/paragraphs (Wikipedia passages) from an external knowledge corpus.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (Wikipedia paragraph corpus per dataset indexed in Elasticsearch/BM25). No agent-written growing memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed-budget recovery of the complete set of gold supporting paragraphs: a maximum of 15 paragraphs is allowed for every retriever system and recall of gold paragraphs within that capped set is measured, i.e. fixed-budget optimal recall rather than a single fixed top-k ranking; the per-step K is tuned for best dev recall.
index_source: Static corpus, constructed offline (per-dataset Wikipedia paragraph corpus indexed in Elasticsearch); not test-time induced and does not grow online.
index_structure_topology: Flat BM25 inverted index (Elasticsearch); no graph or hierarchical structure.
retriever_type: BM25 (sparse lexical), implemented in Elasticsearch; off-the-shelf, no learning.
retriever_learning_signal: None - the base retriever (BM25) is off-the-shelf and not trained; retrieval is steered entirely by the frozen LLM's generated CoT sentences used as queries (no contrastive/RL/preference training of the retriever).
query_construction: Two-phase: (i) initial query is the raw question Q; (ii) thereafter the query is the most recently generated CoT sentence (thought-conditioned query). The LLM generates one CoT sentence at a time conditioned on the question, paragraphs collected so far, and CoT generated so far; only the first generated sentence per reason-step is kept and used as the next retrieval query.
query_granularity: Both task-level and step-level: one task-level query at t=0 (the question), then step/CoT-sentence-level queries at each subsequent iteration.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative - retrieval and reasoning are interleaved on a fixed alternating schedule until a termination criterion (CoT emits 'answer is:' or a max-step threshold, set to 8, is reached).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: a retrieve-step is invoked after every reason-step (each newly generated CoT sentence). There is no confidence/uncertainty/learned-classifier trigger; termination is rule-based ('answer is:' string detected or max steps = 8).
reranking: None - no reranking stage; BM25 top-K paragraphs are added directly (collected paragraphs are capped at 15 total to fit context).
retrieved_context_refinement: None beyond accumulation and capping: paragraphs from all retrieve-steps are collected and de-duplicated/capped at a fixed budget (15); no decompose-recompose, distillation, or distractor filtering of retrieved text.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: collected paragraphs are concatenated into the LLM prompt to (a) guide generation of the next CoT sentence in the retriever loop and (b) be read by a separate QA reader that produces the final answer (CoT Prompting for GPT-3, Direct Prompting for Flan-T5).
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved retrieve-then-reason inside a fixed reasoning loop: alternate reason-step (generate next CoT sentence) and retrieve-step (retrieve K more paragraphs using that sentence) until termination; this is reasoning-guided iterative retrieval rather than tree-search or hierarchical subtask planning.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-CoT-step (per-sentence): retrieval is performed after each generated chain-of-thought sentence.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved paragraphs (verbatim Wikipedia passage text) injected into the prompt; not distilled, summarized, or converted to structured notes.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw document/paragraph (no abstraction or distillation of the retrieved unit).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Implicit/none-trained: robustness comes from step-by-step CoT-guided retrieval (retrieving after each reasoning step reduces early factual errors that derail the CoT) and from including M randomly sampled distractor paragraphs alongside gold paragraphs in the in-context demonstrations so the LLM learns to read amid distractors. No retriever-aware training, relevance evaluator, or self-reflection module.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory; only an accumulating per-question paragraph buffer that resets each question).
write_back: false - the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills; no persistent memory is written across questions.
online_growth: false - the retrievable store (BM25 corpus) is fixed/frozen; it does not grow during deployment.
write_back_trigger: never - no write-back to any persistent store occurs.
failure_experience_usage: N/A - no failure or success experiences are stored or retrieved (no memory). Failures are only analyzed qualitatively (factual-error counts in CoTs), not fed back.
memory_evolution_update: N/A - no stored entries to mutate (no memory).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: false - retrieval/selection is fixed BM25 top-K steered by LLM-generated queries; it is not an RL- or value-optimized retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A - single-model, single-agent; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, IIRC (used in open-domain settings; 100 dev questions for tuning and 500 test questions sampled per dataset).
baselines: One-step Retriever (OneR) and OneR QA; No-Retrieval reader (NoR QA, parametric-only). Leaderboard-style (not head-to-head) comparison against recent few-shot ODQA LLM systems: Internet-Augmented QA (Lazaridou et al. 2022), RECITE (Sun et al. 2022), ReAct (Yao et al. 2022), SelfAsk (Press et al. 2022), and DecomP (Khot et al. 2023). CoT generators: GPT-3 (code-davinci-002, 175B) and Flan-T5 of various sizes (base 0.2B, large 0.7B, XL 3B, XXL 11B).
key_metrics: Retrieval recall of gold paragraphs (fixed-budget, max 15 paragraphs) for the retriever; Answer F1 (and EM) for downstream QA; number of CoTs with >=1 factual error for the hallucination analysis.
headline_result: IRCoT with GPT-3 substantially improves retrieval (up to 21 points recall) and downstream QA (up to 15 points F1) over one-step retrieve-and-read across HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC; e.g., for Flan-T5-XXL IRCoT QA beats OneR QA by +15.3 F1 on 2WikiMultihopQA, and Flan-T5-XL (3B) with IRCoT outperforms the 58x larger GPT-3 with one-step question-based retrieval.
ablations: Model-size scaling study (Flan-T5 base/large/XL/XXL and GPT-3 175B): IRCoT beats OneR on retrieval at all sizes including 0.3B, with the gap roughly growing with model size; IRCoT QA beats OneR QA at all sizes except the smallest 0.3B. Out-of-distribution (OOD) study: using demonstrations from one dataset to evaluate on another preserves the IRCoT advantage in both retrieval and QA. Reader-strategy ablation: Flan-T5 readers do better with Direct Prompting, GPT-3 with CoT Prompting (App. E). Separate reader vs. extracting the answer from the retrieval-time CoT: a separate reader is better (App. F). Hallucination ablation: IRCoT reduces CoT factual errors by ~50% on HotpotQA and ~40% on 2WikiMultihopQA vs OneR (NoR > OneR > IRCoT errors). Hyperparameters: per-step retrieved K and number of distractors M (M in {1,2,3}) tuned on dev.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes - intrinsic retrieval recall is reported separately (Fig. 3/5/8) from end-to-end QA F1/EM (Fig. 4/6/9, Table 1), allowing the retrieval gain to be distinguished from the QA gain.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both: final-outcome QA metrics (F1/EM) plus intermediate process quality via retrieval recall and a CoT factual-error (hallucination) analysis over the generated reasoning chains.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reasoning-cost vs accuracy is discussed qualitatively: IRCoT issues multiple sequential LLM+retrieval calls (one reason-step + one retrieve-step per iteration, max 8 steps) versus a single call for OneR, trading more inference calls/latency for higher recall and QA accuracy; a key efficiency message is that a small 3B IRCoT model matches/beats a 58x larger one-step GPT-3, and gains hold for small models without any training. No explicit token-cost/latency table is reported. [uncertain] exact per-query call counts and dollar/latency figures.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed paragraph budget: collected paragraphs capped at 15 across all retrieve-steps; per-step K tuned over {2,4,6,8} (and OneR's K over {5,7,9,11,13,15}); number of demonstration distractor paragraphs M tuned over {1,2,3}. Context limits: GPT-3 code-davinci-002 ~8K word pieces, Flan-T5 limited to 6K word pieces (memory-bound on 80G A100); demonstrations packed to fill the context.
builds_on: Chain-of-Thought prompting (Wei et al. 2022); few-shot in-context learning / GPT-3 (Brown et al. 2020); the retrieve-and-read open-domain QA paradigm; BM25 (Robertson et al.) in Elasticsearch; Flan-T5 (Chung et al. 2022). Conceptually extends iterative/multi-step retrieval ideas (e.g., GoldEn retriever, multi-hop DPR) to the few-shot prompting setting.
contrasts_with: One-step retrieve-and-read (OneR) and no-retrieval parametric QA (NoR); few-shot ODQA decomposition/action systems SelfAsk, DecomP, ReAct, RECITE, and Internet-Augmented QA, which decompose questions or generate reasoning+action steps but are not developed to improve retrieval via CoT and often need larger models or fine-tuning; supervised iterative-retrieval ODQA methods that require large-scale training (Das et al. 2019, Xiong et al. 2021 multi-hop DPR, GoldEn retriever).
lineage: Group B (retrieval-augmented task solving): an early, influential method establishing CoT-guided iterative/interleaved retrieval for multi-step open-domain QA, a predecessor to later adaptive/iterative RAG (e.g., FLARE, Self-RAG, Adaptive-RAG) that condition when/what to retrieve on the model's intermediate reasoning.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A - not a case-based reasoning method (no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle over solved cases; retrieves documents, not cases).
explicit_cbr_grounding: false - the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite CBR literature (Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner).
tool_document_engineering: N/A - no tools/skills are retrieved; only Wikipedia paragraphs are indexed (raw text via BM25).
index_content_separation: N/A - single flat BM25 paragraph index; no lightweight-index-then-content / progressive-disclosure separation.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A - no tool index or tool-integration protocol; static document corpus only.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A - no inter-tool dependency modeling (no tools).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A - not a CBR method; retrieved paragraphs are used verbatim as in-context evidence, not adapted as cases.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A - this is a method paper, not a survey/taxonomy.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A - this is a method paper, not a benchmark paper; it reuses existing datasets (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, IIRC), sampling 100 dev and 500 test questions per dataset for its experiments.
